name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO)
short_status: Operating: more than 17 years in lunar orbit (NASA, September 16, 2026), now in its sixth extended science mission (October 2025 through September 2028).
tagline: NASA · United States · Orbiter · 2009 · The robotic return Operating

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 18 June 2009, on an Atlas V 401 from Cape Canaveral, riding with the LCROSS impactor

facts.label: Launch date (NASA)
facts.value: 18 June 2009; NASA lists LRO as an active mission and the longest-lived lunar orbiting mission ever

facts.label: Instruments
facts.value: Seven: LROC (imaging, 0.5 m/pixel NAC), LOLA (laser altimeter), Diviner (thermal), LAMP (UV), LEND (neutrons/hydrogen), CRaTER (radiation), Mini-RF (radar)

facts.label: Orbit
facts.value: Polar; ~50 km circular mapping orbit 2009-2011, then an eccentric frozen orbit with periapsis near the south pole to save propellant

facts.label: Current mission phase
facts.value: Extended Science Mission 6 (EM6), October 2025 through September 2028; PI Noah Petro (GSFC); 2025 senior review panel rated the proposal Excellent/Very Good

facts.label: Propellant
facts.value: 10.093 kg usable as of November 2024, sufficient for station-keeping and orbit adjustments through EM6; battery shows some degradation but retains full margin

facts.label: Coldest measured spot
facts.value: Minus 249 C on the permanently shadowed floor of Hermite crater, measured by Diviner in 2009: the coldest temperature ever directly measured in the solar system

facts.label: LROC dataset
facts.value: More than 1.8 petabytes of imaging data supporting Artemis planning (NASA figure, May 2026)

facts.label: LROC operations (new, May 2026)
facts.value: NASA appointed Intuitive Machines prime contractor for LROC operations ($15.5 million cost-plus-fixed-fee, three years) and for ShadowCam operations ($4.5 million, three years) on 18 May 2026 (LROC PI Mark Robinson); IM leads imaging operations, data storage and analysis, and LROC data continues to be distributed through NASA's Planetary Data System

facts.label: Still imaging in 2026
facts.value: LROC PDS release 67C (published 14 September 2026) covers NAC and WAC images acquired May 16 to 15 June 2026

facts.label: Site documentation role
facts.value: LRO has imaged the landing or impact sites of Luna 25 (crash crater, Aug 2023), Chandrayaan-3 (2023), SLIM and Chang'e 6 (2024), Blue Ghost and Athena (Mar 2025), and ispace RESILIENCE (impact, Jun 2025)

timeline: Launched with LCROSS on an Atlas V 401 from Cape Canaveral SLC-41
Entered lunar orbit; commissioning begins
LCROSS Centaur stage impacts Cabeus crater; the experiment confirms water ice at the lunar south pole
Diviner measures minus 249 C in Hermite crater, the coldest temperature directly measured in the solar system
Sep 2010
One-year exploration mission complete; LRO hands over from NASA's exploration directorate to science operations
Low-altitude passes image the Apollo landing sites at about 0.5 m per pixel, resolving hardware and astronaut foot trails
May 2015
Orbit reshaped to an eccentric frozen orbit with low passes (about 20 km) over the south pole
Dec 2015
The modern "Earthrise" composite over Compton crater is released
Aug 2023
Images the fresh crater from Russia's Luna 25 crash, then India's Chandrayaan-3 landing site days later
Mar 2025
Images Firefly's Blue Ghost (within 10 hours of touchdown) and Intuitive Machines' toppled Athena
Jun 2025
Documents the impact site of ispace's RESILIENCE lander in Mare Frigoris
Oct 2025
Sixth extended science mission (EM6) begins, running through September 2028 after an Excellent/Very Good senior-review rating
NASA appoints Intuitive Machines prime contractor for LROC ($15.5M) and ShadowCam ($4.5M) operations, both three-year contracts; LROC data continues through NASA's Planetary Data System
17 years since launch; LRO remains the longest-lived lunar orbiting mission ever
